Billionaire hedge fund manager Bill Ackman on Wednesday took aim at Nvidia’s board of directors, accusing them of "not acting in the best interest of shareholders" in the sudden ouster of CEO Jensen Huang. In a fiery post on X, the Pershing Square Capital Management chief executive argued that the tech giant’s leadership "panicked" over negative headlines rather than conducting proper due diligence. "What we know is that the board fired Jensen or forced his resignation for violating company policy and/or in response to the accusation of an affair with a spy," Ackman wrote. "They did so without careful consideration of the impact on the company, its customers, its shareholders or other stakeholders. They rushed to judgment without the benefit of careful due diligence or even with a basic understanding of the facts." NVIDIA INTERIM CEO SAYS 'WE’VE GOT THIS' AS COMPANY LOOKS TO FUTURE WITHOUT JENSEN HUANG Billionaire hedge fund manager Bill Ackman on Wednesday took aim at Nvidia’s board of directors. (John Lamparski/Bloomberg via Getty Images) Ackman questioned how the board could have properly deliberated on a move with massive implications for shareholders and customers, pointing to the rapid timeline of Huang's exit. "It takes time to convene a board meeting," Ackman said. "There was time, maybe, for one Zoom. And this is a decision that should have been made by a board sitting in person and carefully deliberating the facts once they are known." While acknowledging that corporate boards have the authority to remove a chief executive over an "inappropriate relationship with a subordinate," Ackman said it should not be an "automatic decision." "That is why we have boards comprised of humans and not agents. A board should consider whether or not such a relationship was consensual or whether it was an abuse of power dynamics. And a board has to consider what the impact of the firing is on all stakeholders," Ackman said. Ackman also questioned the legal counsel advising Nvidia's directors, arguing they failed to uphold their "duty of care." "Boards of Delaware companies have a duty of care which means they must make informed, prudent and good faith decisions. This clearly did not happen here," he said. "What law firm is advising this board?" NVIDIA HALTS CHINA AI CHIP SHIPMENTS DESPITE US APPROVAL Ackman further criticized the board for ruling out any possibility of Huang's return. "And now the board is compounding its failures by insisting that there is no possibility for Jensen’s return as CEO. Why is it in the best interest of the company to foreclose the possibility of Jensen’s return and to do so before all of the facts are known?" Ackman questioned. "This is yet another breach of their duty of care." Ackman questioned how the board could have properly deliberated on a move with massive implications for shareholders and customers, pointing to the rapid timeline of Huang's exit.  (Patrick T. Fallon / AFP via Getty Images) He also warned that the board's internal investigation could inflict further damage on the chipmaker. "Furthermore, the board has launched an investigation whose scope is unknown. Investigations can be extremely damaging to a company and should be carefully targeted to address whatever facts need to be known rather than be overly broad in scope," he said. "In short, this looks like a series of major governance failures by directors that panicked due to headlines in the media. They likely felt compelled to do something because they were afraid of looking bad in the media, not because it was the right thing for them company. They couldn’t stand the heat." title: Billionaire investor Bill Ackman bashes Nvidia’s board for not bringing back Jensen Huang - Business Insider
content: Bill Ackman had some strong words for Nvidia's board of directors following the chip giant's earnings report on Tuesday. The billionaire founder of Pershing Square Capital Management  said the board was not acting in the best interests of investors by resisting calls to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang. Huang's sudden resignation from Nvidia over after reports of extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy, has divided the investing community. The company said on Tuesday's earnings call that the board has no plans to bring him back. "I believe the @nvidia board is not acting in the best interest of shareholders nor in a manner consistent with their fiduciary duties," Ackman wrote in an X post on Wednesday. This isn't the first time that Ackman has advocated for Huang to be reinstated. At a recent conference, he outlined a path for the AI stalwart to bring back its former top executive, though he noted that it would hinge on Huang being cleared of any activity related to national security risks. While investigations into Huang's alleged involvement with Chinese tech executive Alice Huang remain ongoing, others seem to share Ackman's sentiment that the former CEO should get his job back. A petition urging Nvidia's board to reinstate him has garnered over 108,000 signatures, including Elon Musk. The campaign's website claims that over 58,000 shareholders and 5,600 company staff members have signed it. Ackman hasn't confirmed if he's one of the signees of the petition, but he said he has problems with how the board handled Huang's departure. "They did so without careful consideration of the impact on the company, its customers, its shareholders or other stakeholders," he said. "They rushed to judgment without the benefit of careful due diligence or even with a basic understanding of the facts." The hedge fund manager added that he based his view on how quickly Huang stepped down following the scandal breaking and how little information the company provided at the time his resignation was announced. In Ackman's opinion, the time allowed for one virtual board meeting at the most, something that he noted often takes time to assemble. The fund manager expressed strong skepticism that the board had enough time to properly assess the facts and decide how to handle what ultimately became Huang's resignation. "And now the board is compounding its failures by insisting that there is no possibility for Jensen's return as CEO," Ackman said. "The board's conduct here is shocking for a company of this scale and importance to our country and the world at large, particularly at this moment in history." Nvidia's board of did not respond to a request for comment on Ackman's statements.

A record quarter wasn’t enough to stop the slide at NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA | NVDA Price Prediction). NVIDIA stock sits at $151.30, down 3% in Wednesday’s afternoon session. That price sits 1.7% above the company’s 52-week low of $148.80. Measured year to date (YTD), NVIDIA stock is down 19%. As recently as October 16, the shares changed hands at $214.13. The selling follows a record quarter and a forecast that topped Wall Street’s expectations, both reported on November 17[1]. Those numbers frame a simple question for NVIDIA. Reaching $100 would require a 33.9% decline from here, while reaching $200 would take a 32.2% climb. With the two levels sitting at similar distances, the next few weeks of news could decide which comes first. NVIDIA’s leadership shake-up is the biggest weight on the stock. Jensen Huang resigned as CEO, and on the company’s November 17[2] earnings call, Chairman Harvey Jones said the board doesn’t intend to reinstate him. Jones stated the board “acted deliberately and in the best interest of the company’s employees, customers, partners, and shareholders.”[2] Longtime CFO Colette Kress is serving as interim CEO while an independent board committee investigation continues. Washington adds a second layer of risk for NVIDIA. Huang is scheduled to appear before the House Foreign Affairs, Intelligence and China Select committees on December 1, and NVIDIA general counsel Tim Teter is due to testify on December 2. Lawmakers have tied the inquiry to concerns that NVIDIA chips sold to a Singapore-based company may have reached China. On November 18, Huang also agreed to appear before the Senate Banking Committee. Interest rates form the third pressure point on NVIDIA. Federal Reserve Bank of New York President John Williams noted on November 17 that surging AI investment point to additional rate hikes next year, a shift that could weigh on highly valued tech stocks. NVIDIA’s business is still expanding at a pace few companies of its scale can match. The company posted record revenue, operating income and earnings per share in Q3 FY2027[2], and Kress called the Vera Rubin rollout “the fastest product ramp in NVIDIA’s history.” Management raised its fiscal 2028 revenue growth outlook on the same call. Wall Street remains firmly in NVIDIA’s corner. Covering analysts set a consensus price target of $267.65. By rating, 10 call the stock a Strong Buy, 49 a Buy, 2 a Hold and 1 a Sell. Leadership clarity could lift the pressure on NVIDIA once the hearings pass. Jones disclosed the board will weigh internal and external candidates[2] for the permanent CEO role. NVIDIA’s closest AI chip rivals are moving the other way. Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) stock is at $522.13, up 4%. On a YTD basis, AMD stock has gained 144%. Broadcom (NASDAQ:AVGO) stock is at $356.10, up 4%. The chipmaker’s YTD gain is a slimmer 3%, still well ahead of NVIDIA’s decline. Gains at both rivals while NVIDIA falls suggest investors are rotating within AI chips and staying with the theme. NVIDIA sells a vertically integrated AI platform including graphics processing units (GPUs), central processing units (CPUs), networking, systems, software and services. The company also reaches beyond the data center into gaming, workstations, automotive, robotics and telecom. AMD pairs its Instinct GPUs with EPYC server CPUs and sells them in Helios rack-scale systems, backed by its open ROCm software stack. Broadcom designs custom AI accelerators and networking chips for hyperscale customers and runs a large infrastructure software business that includes VMware. Each rival competes for the same hyperscale budgets that fund NVIDIA’s data center growth. Both sides of the NVIDIA debate have evidence on the table. The bears can point to an uncertain leadership team, the December hearings in Washington and a rate environment that could weigh on high-multiple tech stocks. title: SpaceX Is Now Nvidia's Biggest Stock Holding, Ahead of Intel. Here's What That Says About SpaceX. - The Motley Fool
content: Is the chipmaker actually betting more on the rocket and AI company? 10 stocks we like better than Space Exploration Technologies › Nvidia (NVDA -2.90%) filed its quarterly list of stock holdings on Monday, Nov. 16, and there's a new name on top. As of Sept. 30, SpaceX (SPCX +1.27%) was the chipmaker's biggest disclosed stake, worth around $19.7 billion, or 40.7% of the reported portfolio. Intel (INTC -0.91%), which led the list three months before, slid to second with 40.1%. Nvidia owned around 130.5 million SpaceX shares at the end of September, up from about 122.8 million at the end of June. Meanwhile, it shrank its Intel stake by a quarter, to around 161.1 million shares. Intel's still the bigger holding by share count. SpaceX leads in value. It's tempting to take this as Nvidia betting more on SpaceX. But I think the filing says less about that than it seems -- and more about how much SpaceX's own plans rely on Nvidia. The filing (a Form 13F, the quarterly holdings report big investment managers send regulators) lists positions on one date. It doesn't say why a position changed. And Nvidia had a way to get more SpaceX shares without buying any. It invested in artificial intelligence (AI) coding firm Cursor in late 2025. SpaceX later bought Cursor in a deal that closed on Aug. 14, paying Cursor's shareholders in SpaceX stock. Some or all of the 7.7 million or so extra shares may have come from the deal. Neither company has said. The bigger shift was on the Intel side. Nvidia's SpaceX stake lost value in the third quarter, dipping from around $21 billion to $19.7 billion as SpaceX's share price dropped. But its Intel stake fell far more, from around $30 billion to $19.4 billion, after Nvidia cut its position by about 54 million shares and Intel's share price slid. Without the extra SpaceX shares, Intel would still have barely kept the top spot. In other words, SpaceX rose to first mainly because Nvidia shrank its Intel stake. For SpaceX, the stake's small. Nvidia's 130.5 million shares made up about 1% of the 13.6 billion or so SpaceX had outstanding in mid-October. At roughly $141 a share as I write, they're worth about $18 billion, versus a market value of about $1.9 trillion. They don't come with much say, either. At the June initial public offering (IPO), CEO Elon Musk had about 82% of the total voting power. The more important tie runs the other way. SpaceX is a big buyer of Nvidia's chips, and its fastest-growing business relies on them. Showing how quickly that business is scaling, SpaceX's super intelligence (SI) segment (its AI cloud services, Grok, Cursor, and X) grew revenue to around $7.6 billion in the third quarter. That's nearly triple the second quarter's $2.6 billion and over nine times the $813 million it took in a year earlier. And the segment swung to $431 million of operating income after losing around $1.3 billion in the second quarter. Its nameplate computing capacity (a measure of the AI chips it's installed) hit 1.7 gigawatts at the end of September, against 1.4 in June and 0.6 in September 2025. Most of SpaceX's capital spending now goes into this build-out. SI took $16.4 billion of the company's third-quarter capital expenditures, or around 84%. "We're tracking to be able to bring roughly 200,000 GB300s online per month for every month for the remainder of this year," Musk said on SpaceX's third-quarter earnings call on Oct. 20. The GB300 is one of Nvidia's AI systems, and Musk said next year's build would be mainly Nvidia's newer Vera Rubin platform. Also, SpaceX's prospectus said its compute deal with Anthropic, which agreed to pay $1.25 billion a month through May 2029, includes around 325,000 Nvidia graphics processing units (GPUs). Of course, Nvidia does fine either way. It makes money when SpaceX buys chips, whether or not those chips end up paying off for SpaceX shareholders. What does Nvidia's filing say about SpaceX, then? Not that the chipmaker is making a big new bet. The stake is around 1% of the company, and it might have grown in the Cursor deal. What it does show is how tightly SpaceX's growth is tied to one supplier's products. At around 33 times the revenue SpaceX would bring in over a year at its third-quarter rate, the stock already assumes those chips pay off. I don't find anything in Nvidia's filing that makes the stock look cheaper. When our analyst team has a stock tip, it can pay to listen. title: Bespoke’s Morning Lineup – 11/18/26 – One Catalyst Down, One to Go - Bespoke Investment Group
content: See what’s driving market performance around the world in today’s Morning Lineup. Bespoke’s Morning Lineup is the best way to start your trading day. Read it now by starting a two-week trial to Bespoke Premium.  CLICK HERE to learn more and start your trial. Below is a snippet of commentary from today’s Morning Lineup. Start a two-week trial to Bespoke Premium to view the full report. With two potential major catalysts looming for investors this week, it looks like we got through the first one unscathed. Nvidia (NVDA) reported an earnings triple play after the close yesterday, and the stock is up nearly 3% in the pre-market. All it has to do now is hang on to those gains, which, lately, has been easier said than done. With NVDA out of the way (for now), investors will shift their focus to the pricing of Anthropic’s (ANT) IPO after the close today. Along with NVDA, equity futures are trading modestly higher. Nasdaq futures are up about 0.5% while the S&P 500 is up a much more modest 0.1%. The Dow, of which NVDA is a member, is poised to open down 0.2%. Treasury yields are trading higher this morning as the 10-year yield climbs above 5.10%. The increase comes on the heels of a CNBC interview with Fed Governor Waller, who just said the Fed may need to “shock” people with a more aggressive policy towards rate hikes as inflation expectations show signs of becoming ingrained at higher levels. Oil prices are trading down about 1%, while gold plunges nearly 3%. In Asia, stocks traded mostly higher, but the gains were muted. The Kospi rallied 2%, but the Nikkei gained only 0.3%, while the Shanghai Composite rose 0.1%. Given the strong results from NVDA, you might have expected larger gains, but investors are still taking a wait-and-see approach to how trade tensions over trade in the technology sector shake out. European stocks have seen little movement in early trading. The STOXX 600 is down 0.1%, led lower by Spain’s 0.5% decline. UK CPI was in line with expectations but still high at 3.6% y/y, while PPI came in much higher than expected, rising 2.2% m/m versus expectations for an increase of just 0.8%. For the Eurozone, October CPI increased 0.5%, which was ahead of the 0.4% forecast. Today will be a busy day for economic data, with Building Permits and Housing Starts at 8:30 followed by Pending Home Sales at 10 AM. Housing Starts managed to exceed forecasts, but permits missed forecasts by a wide margin. We’ll also get the release of minutes from October’s meeting. There are also several Fed officials scheduled to speak, which kicked off with Waller’s relatively hawkish comments on CNBC earlier. Since NVDA’s earnings release last night, we’ve read a few comments suggesting that if the company didn’t have the issues surrounding Jensen Huang and potential illicit sales of chips to China acting as an overhang, shares would be performing much better in the pre-market. We can never know what the results of a counterfactual would be, but just based on the stock’s reaction to its last eight earnings reports, there is little to suggest that NVDA’s stock would be doing better in reaction to earnings. The table below shows the results of NVDA’s last eight earnings reports and how the stock performed on its earnings reaction day. In the last two years, NVDA reported better-than-expected EPS and sales every quarter, raised guidance five times, and lowered guidance just once. Despite those stellar results relative to expectations, NVDA only reacted positively to earnings three times. After the five triple plays, the stock fell in reaction to earnings four times. With a gain of close to 3% in the pre-market, NVDA’s results today would rank as the third best relative to the last two years. So much for an overhang. So, is the market looking past Jensen Huang and seeing bright skies ahead for NVDA? We wouldn’t say that. Heading into last night’s report, NVDA was down 36% from its record high on 10/6. This morning, the stock is down 34% from that high. There is nothing to suggest that interim CEO Colette Kress hasn’t “got this,” but the company still has a long road ahead to assure investors. Last night’s results all covered a period before the Huang scandal broke, and orders for this quarter and even next year were likely already booked. With NVDA’s report out of the way, we’re at the tail end of earnings season, which is a period when the retailers start to report. Yesterday, we heard from Home Depot (HD), today Lowe’s (LOW) and TJX reported, and tomorrow we’ll get Walmart’s (WMT) results which typically marks the unofficial end to earnings season. With inflation running hot, and gas prices hitting consumers in the wallet, retail stocks have held up relatively well. The S&P Retail ETF (XRT), which weights each of its components equally, has pulled back from 52-week highs in the last week but remains right on the edge of overbought territory. Last week, it also completed a golden cross, which occurs when the 50-day moving average crosses up through the 200-day moving average as both are rising. As the chart above illustrates, XRT has been largely rangebound over the last year. One result of the lack of headway has been a lot of oscillation between the 50 and 200-DMAs, and as a result, last week’s golden cross was the second in the last four months. Crossovers between the two moving averages tend to occur relatively infrequently, so two upside crosses in such a short period of time is uncommon. Golden crosses are considered positive technical formations, but as we’ve highlighted in the past, actual results don’t often back up that idea. The table below shows XRT’s performance following its 12 prior golden crosses since 2006. Overall, results were positive. While performance looking out over the next three months was basically a coin flip, six- and twelve-month returns were positive nearly three quarters of the time. title: Chart of the Day: A Look at Nvidia After Earnings - RealMoney Pro
content: Too much turmoil and potential liability sees big money slowly exit. We can talk about valuation all we want with Nvidia (NVDA), how cheap the stock looks into the next couple of years. If you believe in 2028 the company will make $20 in earnings (prior modeled guidance) then the stock is trading at 8 times expected earnings for that year, growing better than 50%. That is dirt cheap, but here we are post earnings. Nvidia put up good numbers, yet there is this dark cloud over the company that won’t just quickly disappear. The stories and the rhetoric surrounding the company are never ending and the spin changes each day. But what does not change is the chart, which is bearish. The top pane shows purple bars, bearish on the GoNoGo composite of indicators. No need to be aggressive and catch a falling knife here. ADX is strong, telling us the trend is very powerful. If the stock stops coming down this indicator will start to fall, not to bullish but probably less bearish. Money flows remain negative. The top chart shows heavy volume to the downside, big distribution in the name, which means large institutions are selling, not buying. We still like Nvidia for the long term in TheStreet Pro Portfolio and rate it a One, or “buy at anytime.”  In fact, we picked up a bit more this morning. title: Nvidia (NVDA Stock) Posts Record $115.8 Billion Revenue as AI Boom Raises Emissions Concerns - CarbonCredits.com
content: Nvidia has reported record quarterly revenue of US$115.8 billion, more than doubling its sales from a year earlier as demand for artificial intelligence (AI) chips continues to grow. The results beat Wall Street estimates and came with a stronger outlook for the next quarter, showing that spending on AI infrastructure remains strong. However, the earnings report also arrives during a major leadership crisis. Co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as CEO and board member on November 12. During its November 17 earnings call, Nvidia’s board confirmed that it does not intend to reinstate him. Beyond its financial growth, Nvidia faces another challenge: managing the rising environmental impact of AI. Its latest sustainability report shows a sharp increase in supply chain emissions, even as the company matches all its operational electricity use with clean energy. This raises questions about whether its climate targets can keep pace with the rapid expansion of AI computing. Nvidia reported revenue of $115.8 billion for the third quarter of fiscal 2027, which ended October 25. This was a 103% increase from $57 billion a year earlier and 20% higher than the previous quarter. Net income rose 105% year-over-year to $65.3 billion. Earnings per diluted share reached $2.70 on a GAAP basis, up 108% from $1.30 in the same quarter last year. Non-GAAP earnings per share climbed 111% to $2.68. The company’s data center business remained the main growth driver. Revenue from this segment reached $107.6 billion, up 110% from a year earlier. It accounted for about 93% of total quarterly sales, reflecting strong demand for AI processors and computing systems. Nvidia also reported a gross margin of 74.8% on a GAAP basis. This was slightly below the 75% recorded in the previous quarter but above the 73.4% reported a year earlier. The company returned $28.1 billion to shareholders through share buybacks and dividends during the quarter. It also had $227.3 billion remaining under its share repurchase authorization at the end of the period. These results show how quickly Nvidia has grown as companies invest in AI data centers and computing infrastructure. However, the scale of its dependence on data center demand also makes the company sensitive to any slowdown in AI spending. Colette Kress, interim CEO and Executive VP and CFO of Nvidia, remarked: “Our momentum is real. NVIDIA is an exceptional technology leader, powered by the relentless innovation of our people. Vera Rubin is off to an explosive start, our roadmap is on track, and our ambition has never been greater.” Nvidia expects fourth-quarter fiscal 2027 revenue to reach $130 billion, with a possible range of $126.1 billion to $133.9 billion. This is above the market’s average forecast of just over $125 billion. The outlook is notable because Nvidia said it does not expect any data center computing revenue from China during the quarter. This suggests that demand from other markets could support its growth even without sales to China. Interim CEO and CFO Colette Kress also told investors that Nvidia expects revenue to grow 75% in fiscal 2028. The company has begun shipping its new Vera Rubin NVL72 computing systems, which it described as the fastest product ramp in its history. Still, investors must consider the leadership change. Huang resigned on November 12 after the company disclosed that his personal conduct was inconsistent with its code of conduct and workplace standards. The board unanimously accepted his resignation and appointed Kress as interim CEO while it searches for a permanent replacement. The issue became more significant on November 17, when Huang publicly said he would be honored to return if the board believed it was in the company’s best interest. However, board chair Harvey C. Jones said during the earnings call that the board does not intend to reinstate him. Nvidia also said it would not take questions about Huang’s resignation during the call. The board has formed a committee to oversee national security and export-control issues, adding another layer of scrutiny to the company’s governance. Nvidia (NVDA) stock gained about 5% in after-hours trading on November 17 following the earnings release, as investors welcomed the stronger-than-expected revenue forecast and improved growth outlook. The rebound came after the stock had fallen roughly 10% since Huang’s resignation, reflecting concerns about the leadership change and its potential impact on the company. Despite the leadership turmoil, Nvidia’s results suggest that its business remains strong. However, the search for a permanent CEO will test whether the company can maintain its product roadmap, customer relationships, and growth without its longtime leader. Nvidia’s financial growth reflects the rapid expansion of AI infrastructure. Still, more powerful computing systems also require more electricity, cooling, and materials. The company’s fiscal 2026 sustainability report shows that its total reported Scope 3 emissions reached 10.7 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent (MtCO2e). This was about 55% higher than the 6.9 MtCO2e reported in FY2025 and nearly three times the 3.6 MtCO2e recorded in FY2024. Purchased goods and services accounted for the largest share, at 9.3 MtCO2e. Capital goods added another 955,000 tonnes. These figures highlight the emissions linked to manufacturing chips, servers, and other equipment across Nvidia’s supply chain. Nvidia also reported 308,891 tonnes of location-based Scope 2 emissions in FY2026, up from 228,378 tonnes a year earlier. This measures emissions linked to the electricity mix in the regions where the company operates. The figures need some context. Nvidia is a fabless chip company, meaning it does not own the manufacturing plants that produce its chips. Much of its environmental footprint therefore comes from suppliers and other parts of its value chain. The Scope 3 total in its published emissions table covers categories 1 to 8. It should not be confused with a complete estimate of all emissions linked to the use of its sold products. Nvidia says it matched 100% of its global electricity consumption with clean electricity for sites under its operational control in FY2026. It used on-site solar, power purchase agreements, renewable electricity tariffs, and energy attribute certificates to meet this goal. However, this does not mean all its facilities physically run on renewable power at all times. The company has also adopted two emissions targets validated by the Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi). From a fiscal 2023 baseline, it aims to: Nvidia is also promoting liquid cooling and more efficient data center designs. These technologies can reduce cooling needs and improve computing performance per unit of energy. However, total electricity demand may still rise as AI use expands. The company reported about 1.05 million megawatt-hours of energy consumption in FY2026, up from 816,000 MWh a year earlier. It also reported 451,297 cubic meters of water withdrawal, although changes in data collection limit comparisons with previous years. The International Energy Agency has warned that growing data center demand will put more pressure on power systems. This makes cleaner electricity, stronger grids, and better energy efficiency increasingly important. Nvidia’s latest earnings show that the AI boom continues to generate exceptional revenue and profits. Its strong outlook also suggests that demand for AI chips and data center systems could remain high. However, rising Scope 3 emissions show the environmental cost of this growth. Matching operational electricity use with clean energy and improving chip efficiency are important steps, but they do not fully address emissions from manufacturing and the wider AI supply chain. title: NVDA Stock Set For Fifth Day Lower: House Committee Goes Steps Up Nvidia Investigation, Asks Kress To Testify - TradingView
content: A congressional committee demanded Wednesday that semiconductor giant Nvidia provide a formal briefing regarding alleged export control violations and former chief executive Jensen Huang’s relationship with a suspected Chinese spy. Representative Brett Guthrie, chairman of the House Committee on Energy and Commerce, sent a letter to Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress requesting company officials appear before the panel no later than December. 2. The committee is investigating whether Nvidia bypassed federal restrictions designed to keep advanced artificial intelligence technology out of China, as well as whether a top company official attempted to interfere with a federal inquiry. "These reported events raise questions about the company's compliance with existing federal law regarding the export of advanced technologies, as well as the robustness and efficacy of the company's security controls," Guthrie wrote in the letter. The congressional inquiry centers on Megaspeed, a Singapore-based Nvidia customer suspected of helping Chinese firms circumvent U.S. export bans. On November 16, the Justice Department and the Commerce Department publicly confirmed they are conducting a joint criminal investigation into Megaspeed. Federal scrutiny intensified following reports that Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, who is the alleged Chinese spy romantically linked with Jensen Huang, built a network of companies across China and Singapore to acquire Nvidia hardware. According to Guthrie's letter, lawmakers are also examining allegations that the Commerce Department handed its initial probe of Megaspeed over to the Justice Department last year after Nvidia’s general counsel contacted Commerce officials seeking details about the inquiry. The mounting scandal has already triggered major leadership changes at the Santa Clara, California-based tech giant. On November 8, Jensen Huang sent an internal email to staff acknowledging an extramarital affair and stating that Nvidia's board of directors had launched an independent investigation into the national security concerns raised by media reports. Four days later, on November 12, he announced his resignation from company leadership. Kress, who previously served as Nvidia's chief financial officer, stepped in as interim CEO while the company works with an external firm to search for a permanent replacement. Ever since the controversy erupted, Nvidia’s stock has been on a consistent downward spiral with its shares on track to end its seventh consecutive week lower. The Energy and Commerce Committee, which holds jurisdiction over interstate and foreign commerce also requested appearances from Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and his deputy Jeffrey Kessler who are overseeing chip export controls. The letter arrived just one day after three other House committees announced that Jensen Huang and Nvidia's general counsel are scheduled to brief lawmakers early next month. Huang will appear before the House Foreign Affairs Committee, the Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, and the House Intelligence Committee on December 1, while Nvidia’s General Counsel Tim Teter will appear before the committees on December 2. Maybe Nvidia (NVDA) doesn't need a big free-agent CEO signing to replace highly visible founder and former CEO Jensen Huang. "If you don't bring Jensen back, I would not hire an outsider," Amazon (AMZN) founder and former CEO Jeff Bezos said at a Semafor conference on Tuesday. "Nvidia is too complicated. I think outside CEOs in complex companies have a vanishingly small chance of succeeding." A new CEO often comes in and runs the standard playbook from an MBA class: Do a listening tour with employees to better understand the business. Meet with the existing C-suite to see who they want to keep and who should get pushed out. Six months into the job, the new CEO unveils a splashy growth plan that often includes profit-boosting layoffs. The thing is, Nvidia doesn't need any of this playbook inserted into its unique culture Huang created. It also doesn't need its important operations disrupted by a meddling new CEO seeking praise from the world. At best, Nvidia needs an internal CEO hire — someone with Huang's technical prowess who could sell the sizzle to a global audience. At worst, it needs a big-name veteran CEO who promises the board no major overhauls, just small tweaks where needed. That person stays in the job for a few years and establishes a strong succession plan — one that Huang never whipped up. For his part, Bezos and his board named then-AWS leader and longtime Amazon exec Andy Jassy to succeed him as CEO in 2021. "I don't think it needs a big splashy hire. I think they have incredible bench strength in there," investor and "Shark Tank" star Kevin O'Leary said on Sozzi Unleashed. "I think they have a tremendous amount of engineers designing the next two generations of chips. I think it's a machine unto itself right now." Interim CEO Colette Kress made a solid case late Tuesday for staying in the interim CEO role for perhaps longer than Wall Street expects. The company's third quarter was solid, the outlook strong, and Kress came across as a steady hand driving the Nvidia rocketship. For the third quarter, Nvidia posted adjusted earnings of $2.68 a share on revenue of $115.8 billion. Wall Street had expected earnings of $2.47 a share on revenue of $109.15 billion. Nvidia expects fourth quarter revenue of $127.4 billion to $132.6 billion, comfortably above the $125.25 billion analysts were looking for. The company said it sees fiscal year 2028 revenue growth of 75%, up from a prior estimate of 70% offered just three months ago. "Although no one can truly replace Mr. Huang, our takeaway from the call is that it will remain business as usual, and the company will continue executing despite the sudden shake up," D.A. Davidson analyst Gil Luria said. "We are encouraged by the FY28 guidance raise, something we do not think would have been done without confidence from management. title: Another short-seller announces a bet against Nvidia over possible ties to China - Business Insider
content: Another short-seller is betting against Nvidia over problems it sees with alleged ties to China. Muddy Waters, the activist short-seller run by Carson Block, unveiled a bearish bet ahead of the chip giant's earnings on Tuesday. The firm's report centers around an ongoing class action complaint filed in October in California against Super Micro Computer, a company that makes servers and other hardware for AI systems. The suit claims that an executive named Cenly Chen had knowledge of illicit sales of Nvidia chips to China. Muddy Waters points to Chen and a potential connection to former Nvidia executive Ajay Puri. The two have been photographed together numerous times over the years, though neither Muddy Waters' report nor the lawsuit directly accuse Puri or Nvidia of any wrongdoing. "A woman identified as Cenly Chen, referred to in some photograph tags as Cenly Puri, has been photographed in public between 2024 to 2026 with Ajay K. Puri. Until this June, Mr. Puri was likely the third most senior executive at NVDA, behind only Jensen Huang and Colette Kress," the firm's report reads. The Information reported on Wednesday that Puri and Chen are married, as disclosed to work colleagues. A representative for Muddy Waters said that the report corroborates the firm's thesis about their connection. Nvidia did not respond to a request for comment. Super Micro Computer issued the following statement regarding Muddy Waters' report to Business Insider: "Cenly Chen did not manage Supermicro's relationship with Nvidia and did not decide how Nvidia GPUs were distributed to customers," a spokesperson said. "After 18 years at Supermicro, Ms. Chen voluntarily resigned in early 2026 to take the CEO role at ChronoScale." Muddy Waters said that Super Micro Computer did not respond to requests to confirm if the woman photographed was the same Cenly Chen who held roles at the firm, including as chief growth officer and managing director. Add BI in Google so our reporting is easier to find when you’re searching for what matters. Super Micro Computer has come under legal scrutiny in the past. In March 2026, one of its co-founders was part of a group arrested for illegally smuggling AI chip components into China. "In March this year, the U.S. indicted three individuals associated with SMCI, including a co-founder, for illegally selling at least approximately $2.5 billion of SMCI servers with NVDA GPUs to end customers in China through a Southeast Asian front company," the Muddy Waters report states. It added that a former Super Micro Computer executive stated in the lawsuit that there was "no way Cenly Chen lacked knowledge of [SMCI's] illicit sales." This is the first time that Muddy Waters has announced a short position against the AI leader. The claims in its report aren't framed as wrongdoing on Nvidia's part. At a time when investors are still focused on the fallout from Huang's alleged ties to Chinese tech executive Alice Huang, Puri's potential connection to Chen could raise more negative speculation as the chip leader tries to get back on its feet. Muddy Waters CEO Carson Block said that his call is not based on a view of Nvidia's fundamentals or valuation. title: TradeXYZ leads NVDA perpetual open interest at $222.1M on Hyperliquid - Crypto Briefing

The venue's Nvidia-tracking contract holds a commanding lead over rival Hyperliquid markets as traders position around earnings Wed 18 Nov 2026 · 08:40 EST
·
                            3 min read TradeXYZ’s Nvidia perpetual contract now carries $222.1 million in open interest. The next-largest Hyperliquid venue offering the same exposure sits at $5.1 million. The contract in question is xyz:NVDA, a perpetual futures market designed to track the share price of Nvidia Corporation, which trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker NVDA. It lives on Hyperliquid, a blockchain built around on-chain derivatives trading. Open interest measures the total value of contracts that remain open at a given moment. It is not trading volume. It captures how much money is actively parked in positions, waiting to win or lose. On that metric, xyz:NVDA reached $222.1 million as of mid-November 2026, according to the research findings. The closest competitor, identified in the research as Entropy’s io:NVDA, held roughly $5 million. Trading activity looks just as lopsided in TradeXYZ’s favor. Recent 24-hour volumes on xyz:NVDA have ranged between $480 million and $1 billion. The xyz:NVDA contract references one share of Nvidia common stock. It settles in cash using USDC, the dollar-pegged stablecoin, rather than delivering any actual shares. Holders get price exposure to Nvidia, but no ownership, no voting rights and no dividends. Daily. Free. Join 34,000+ readers across crypto, finance, and policy. To keep the contract’s price anchored to Nvidia’s real share price, the market uses a funding rate. These are periodic payments between traders on the long and short sides that nudge the perpetual back toward the underlying asset. On xyz:NVDA, funding is charged hourly, with rates typically set between 5% and 10% on an annualized basis. The contract also trades 24/7, a notable departure from Nasdaq, which closes on evenings and weekends. On November 16, 2026, TradeXYZ halved the maximum leverage available on xyz:NVDA, from 20x down to 10x. The timing stands out. Nvidia’s earnings report was scheduled for November 17 to 18, according to the research findings, which suggest the leverage reduction was likely made ahead of that event as a risk management step. Notably, the lower leverage cap does not appear to have dampened appetite. Volumes stayed in the hundreds of millions of dollars per day after the change. TradeXYZ launched its HIP-3 deployment on Hyperliquid in October 2025. HIP-3 refers to the framework under which multiple venues, TradeXYZ and Entropy among them, list their own markets on the Hyperliquid chain. Over roughly a year, TradeXYZ has expanded beyond a single product to offer a range of equity perpetuals. The research describes the venue as having captured significant market share quickly after launch. For Hyperliquid’s HIP-3 ecosystem, the data points to a winner-take-most dynamic. When one venue holds $222.1 million in open interest and the runner-up holds $5.1 million, liquidity is concentrating in a single place. For traders, the appeal is clear: round-the-clock access, leverage, and stablecoin settlement on a stock that dominates market conversation. The trade-offs are just as real. There are no shareholder rights, funding costs accrue every hour, and the platform can change leverage terms, as the November 16 adjustment showed. title: Nvidia Delivers, but the Response Is Muted. Here’s How I’m Playing It. - RealMoney Pro
content: The report reduced some uncertainty, and the stock should find support while the focus shifts to the Anthropic IPO. Registering unlocks your remaining free Pro articles. The Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) is up about 1% and the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY) 0.6% early Wednesday following a limited, but favorable response to the earnings report from Nvidia (NVDA). Nvidia’s results were strong and surpassed most expectations. Revenue more than doubled from a year ago to about $116 billion, and the forecast of $130 billion for the current quarter was better than expected. Interim CEO Colette Kress raised the growth projection for next year to 75% from 70% and said that “from a business perspective, it’s business as usual.” The company also said that Jensen Huang will not be coming back as CEO. Nvidia stock is up about 3.7% in early premarket trading. For a report this good, in a stock that has lost a third of its value, that isn’t much. We’ll see if it attracts more interest as we move toward the opening bell. There is skepticism, and there is some concern that the drama at the company may empower the competition. Judson Althoff, who runs the commercial business at Microsoft (MSFT), said the turmoil could prompt customers to consider alternatives to Nvidia’s chips and that some are “waiting for the dust to settle,” according to Bloomberg. Microsoft, Amazon (AMZN) and Alphabet (GOOGL) are all developing their own AI chips to reduce their dependence on Nvidia. Kress also indicated that Nvidia will continue to finance data-center construction for its customers, and that is helping the smaller data-center companies like Nebius Group (NBIS) and CoreWeave (CRWV) Wednesday morning. The questions about circular financing, and the SEC investigation reported on Tuesday, aren’t going away. The key now is for the stock to hold the low around $150 and build a new base of support. That will set up the right technical conditions for a bigger buy with a clear stop level. I continue to hold my small position while I wait for that to develop, and I’m in no hurry. A base takes time to form, and I’d rather pay a little more for a stock that has proven it can hold than guess at it this morning. The focus will now shift to the Anthropic IPO, and indications are that there is strong demand. The Wall Street Journal reports that the company expects to price its shares above the planned range, possibly at more than $80, which would value it at $1.5 trillion to $1.6 trillion. The pricing is expected Wednesday, and the stock is scheduled to start trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday. If it trades well, that will give the market further support and set up a foundation for some positive end-of-the-year seasonality to start to build. I don’t want to be overly optimistic at this point. More than 700 stocks hit new lows Tuesday, and one good open doesn’t repair that. However, the Nvidia report has helped to reduce uncertainty to some extent, and that is what was needed. There are still some significant headwinds, especially interest rates, and we have the minutes of the last Fed meeting Wednesday afternoon. Oil is lower again this morning, and bonds are ticking higher, which helps. I’ll be looking harder to put more capital to work, but incrementally and with tight stops. title: Colette Kress Just Delivered Excellent News for Nvidia Investors - The Motley Fool
content: Nvidia passed its earnings call with flying colors. AI investors and beyond were eagerly anticipating Nvidia's (NVDA -2.90%) earnings call Tuesday night. The earnings report was the company's first since Jensen Huang stepped down as CEO amid controversy last week. Nvidia named CFO Colette Kress as the interim CEO as it conducts a search for a permanent replacement, considering both internal and external candidates. Kress passed her first test with flying colors, as she delivered a confident pitch for the company and even raised guidance for fiscal 2028 from 70% revenue growth to 75% revenue growth. Nvidia also beat estimates on the top and bottom lines, and the stock was trading higher after the call, up 3.3% as of 8:23 p.m. However, amid the focus on the headline numbers and parsing the call for hints into the company's future, there was one key comment from Kress that investors may have missed. It's understandable why Nvidia is down a third from its peak last month, given Huang's sudden exit, but with Nvidia stock now trading at a forward P/E of just 11, the stock is as cheap as it's ever been and ripe for share buybacks. In response to a question about the company's capital allocation and its buyback plans, Kress said that the "super top priority" for returning capital to shareholders was to use the company's current share repurchase authorization, which was raised by $150 billion in September and sat at $227.3 billion at the end of the third quarter. Kress added, "So thinking about all of that together, I think there is definitely room to continue all of the stock repurchase plans that we want to do and complete those before the end of fiscal year '28." She also noted that the top priority for its capital spending is supporting its suppliers in building out additional capacity. If Nvidia executes on those buybacks and the stock price stays roughly the same, it would reduce shares outstanding by roughly 6% by Jan. 2028, when fiscal 2028 ends. When the Total Conviction signal flashed for Nvidia in 2009, most people ignored it. The ones who acted turned $5,000 into $2,799,718*. Now, for the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. It’s a key player in the $1.8 trillion space race, and with the stock recently sitting 20% off its highs, the window to get in early is closing fast. The share repurchase authorization and Kress's commitment are a positive sign, not just because it will lift Nvidia's earnings per share, but because it shows management's confidence that the stock is undervalued after the recent sell-off and signals to investors that it's worth buying. For investors worried that Nvidia would struggle during the transitional period, Kress gave no indication that anything has changed, saying, "it's business as usual," and that customers, suppliers, and partners are all "100% behind us." Demand for the company's products continues to outstrip supply, and Kress spent much of the call reiterating the company's commitment to securing adequate supply, which allowed it to raise its revenue guidance for fiscal 2028. In just one quarter, its supply commitments increased from $279 billion, primarily due to memory supply. Kress said, "We feel confident in terms of both the demand that we have in front of us as well as the supply and additionally that we can do the 75%," referring to 75% revenue growth next year. Nvidia also addressed the controversy around Jensen Huang, and new Chairman of the Board Harvey Jones made it clear that the board has no intention of reinstating Huang. Regarding the CEO search, Jones said, "We want to install this CEO, the permanent CEO, as quickly as possible, but we won't expedite the CEO before finding exactly the right person." Ian Buck, Nvidia's vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing, who has been seen as a possible replacement for Huang, was on the Q&A portion of the call, but did not answer any questions. Nvidia did what it needed to do on the earnings call and then some. Its commitment to using up its $227 billion share repurchase authorization and the guidance hike for fiscal 2028 show investors the company continues to excel. Nvidia is on track to bring in more than $700 billion in revenue next year. Given the deep discount, Nvidia looks like a buy, even without Jensen Huang. In its highly anticipated earnings release Tuesday, Nvidia said third-quarter revenue doubled to more than $115 billion, generating a net profit of $65.3 billion. The firm also increased its forecast for next year's revenue to 75 percent growth. But investors also noted that the United States moved to tighten restrictions on Chinese access to chips, while Huang has agreed to meet US lawmakers on December 1 to answer questions about national security concerns. "For Nvidia, strong earnings have bought management time," said Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at Saxo. "For the broader AI trade, they reinforce confidence in infrastructure demand, but the next leg of the rally may depend increasingly on which companies can turn that demand into sustainable profits." Interim CEO Colette Kress said it was "business as usual" after the loss of Huang, a pivotal player in the eye-watering growth of the artificial intelligence industry. But the US markets were unforgiving for Nvidia, whose shares fell by 2.9 percent by the close in New York, continuing a run of weeks of heavy losses and in keeping with a slump across two of the three main US indexes on Wednesday, with the Nasdaq the only one to close in the green. European bourses also slipped into the red by close of play, as did most markets in Asia. Analysts noted that many investors were likely reducing their holdings in other stocks to free up funds to buy shares in Anthropic. "Investors are preparing for a blowout IPO tomorrow from Anthropic," said Peter Cardillo from Spartan Capital Securities. "Hopefully (it) might begin to alleviate some of the worries that the market is undergoing." The five-year-old startup is going public Thursday in an IPO that could raise $65 billion or more -- giving investors a first chance to bet directly on a stand-alone AI giant in a test of how long the sector's spending boom can last. "The issue is over six times subscribed, and there's plenty of excitement ahead of the first public offering of a pure frontier lab at the forefront of AI development," said David Morrison, senior market analyst at Trade Nation. Anthropic is widely seen as the leader for AI products, while Nvidia has been dubbed the "central bank" of the industry for its investments in start-ups and providing backstops on loans. On currency markets, the dollar extended its recent gains against major rivals on expectations the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates next month and possibly again early next year. That could slow economic growth, but it would raise returns on US government bonds, considered one of the safest investments available. On Wednesday, minutes from the Fed's last meeting in October showed that "almost all" policymaker expected further hikes to be necessary, with Governor Chris Waller telling US broadcaster CNBC he could back a 50-basis-point increase. The Santa Clara chip giant said it was looking for a replacement for the former chief executive and declined to answer questions about Huang during a conference call after its latest earnings report on Tuesday. Nvidia's leadership has been in flux after Huang resigned and admitted to an extramarital affair with a Chinese businesswoman who U.S. intelligence officials believe is a Chinese spy. Other affairs, including with an Nvidia employee, have surfaced since. "The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO," Harvey C. Jones, Nvidia's chairman, said in an opening statement. "While this was an unexpected transition, the board acted deliberately and in the best interest of the company's employees, customers, partners, and shareholders." The company's stance came amid growing calls to hire back Jensen. Jensen himself said this week that he would be willing to return as CEO if the board invited him back. "Since my departure, I've seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA's employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO," Huang wrote in an X post. "If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO." The company reported record profits of $116 billion for the quarter that ended in September, doubling from last year. The revenue beat analyst expectations of $109 billion, reinforcing the strong demand for AI applications. It raised its growth outlook for the coming quarter and year. Nvidia shares, which have tumbled 20% so far this year, climbed around 4% in after-hours trading Tuesday after the earnings announcement. The stock price was near $160 in early after-hours trading. "The tone of the call sent the message that Nvidia is moving forward without Jensen Huang without saying so explicitly," said Jacob Bourne, analyst at Emarketer. "Interim CEO Colette Kress led that message, projecting optimism, confidence, and a clear sense of direction for the company's future." The board has launched an investigation into Huang's affair and said it does not believe Huang divulged Nvidia secrets or compromised national security. The board appointed longtime Chief Financial Officer Kress as interim chief executive. In response to a surge in security concerns, the Nvidia board said Tuesday that it has formed a committee to oversee compliance with national security and export controls for its advanced chips, a focus that has come into sharp relief in Washington. "This committee will enhance our engagement with the U.S. government, including all relevant agencies," Jones said. Huang is a central figure of the AI boom, whose advanced semiconductor chips underpin 90% of the global market. Through savvy dealmaking and by bankrolling smaller startups, he turned Nvidia into a $5-trillion colossus. This created an extremely loyal employee base, many of whom want him to return, increasing pressure on the new management to ease fears and prevent potential employee churn. "We will take care of our employees during this transition to make sure that they are safe and making sure the work can be done in the current environment," Kress said. Huang advocated relaxing export controls on advanced chips to China, arguing that cutting off access would only accelerate China's resolve to build domestic alternatives. He leveraged his relationship to President Trump to overturn a Biden-era export ban and sold less powerful chips to Chinese customers, in exchange for a percentage of sales revenue going to the U.S. government. Nvidia has lost nearly $2 trillion in market value since his departure. Over the weekend, Huang's allies in Silicon Valley started a "Stand with Jensen," campaign demanding his return. The letter received over 100,000 signatures, including from employees, and support from Tesla Chief Executive Elon Musk. Trump also reposed his faith in Huang since the affair first surfaced, and earlier this week said that he "would not mind" if he returned. title: Prediction: These Will Be Nvidia’s and AMD’s Stock Prices by the End of 2027 (Hint: Only 1 Is a Buy). - The Motley Fool
content: AMD's stock has a ton of growth priced into it already. Nvidia (NVDA -2.90%) has had a rough few weeks with CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang resigning. That has cratered the stock, which is now down significantly from its all-time high. Nvidia's loss has been AMD's (AMD +5.31%) gain. The rival chipmaker’s stock has risen 16% since November began, while Nvidia's is down nearly 20%. AMD investors couldn't have been more pleased. There's also the potential that some Nvidia investors are shifting funds into AMD shares to maintain their AI exposure without the mess of a CEO transition, which is a valid premise. However, I think most of the Nvidia saga will be wrapped up by the time 2027 ends, and the stock market will have returned to valuing both businesses for what they are, rather than based on how headlines are influencing them. So, what do I expect each stock to be trading at by the end of 2027? I think you'll be very surprised. Leadership matters in a company. That's why the news of Huang’s rapid exit was so jarring to many investors. He has been the only CEO in its history, and he was instrumental in building the company into what it is today. Without him at the helm, some investors aren't as confident in Nvidia's prospects. Still, Huang didn't do everything at Nvidia. Countless others helped build Nvidia into what it is, many of its longtime leaders are still there, and one could take over next. Nvidia's products remain superior to AMD's, and the company still has a wide moat thanks to the ubiquity of its CUDA software platform, which allows its GPUs to be programmed for whatever uses its customers have in mind. Because so much early AI work was done on CUDA, and because so many developers are comfortable in it, shifting out of the Nvidia ecosystem can be a chore. While AMD's GPUs are growing more popular, they're only being deployed in certain applications. Meanwhile, Nvidia still holds a commanding market-share lead in data center GPUs and is still delivering faster sales growth. NVDA Revenue (Quarterly YoY Growth) data by YCharts Nvidia has recently delivered particularly impressive growth given how large its revenue base is relative to AMD's, but the market isn't giving the chipmaker credit for it. With 2026 nearly wrapped up, it's OK for investors to start looking ahead to 2027. Next year, Wall Street analysts expect Nvidia's revenue to grow at a 67% pace. While some may discount that growth rate given what's going on in the C-suite, I don't think that's a wise investment move. The reality is that Nvidia's largest clients already know what they're going to spend on chips next year, and they've let Nvidia know so these products are ready to go when they need them. During the Q2 earnings call, management gave guidance for 70% revenue growth in 2027. It's rare to see a company issue guidance for the upcoming year so far in advance. The only reason why Nvidia would do that is if it had high visibility into revenue, and nothing that has happened over the past few weeks will likely change its outlook for 2027. According to the analyst community, AMD's growth rate is expected to exceed Nvidia's. Analysts project AMD will grow its revenue at an 84% clip. That would be a strong outperformance if AMD can pull it off, but considering its much smaller sales base, it's not growing nearly fast enough to make a big dent in Nvidia's lead. Regardless of what transpires next year, the reality is that AMD's expected growth has already been priced into its stock, while Nvidia's hasn't. AMD is over three times more expensive than Nvidia based on next year's earnings projections. That's a huge price mismatch, and I think it's a bit absurd that AMD trades at that much of a premium when their growth rates are fairly similar. While I agree that AMD deserves a premium right now because its CEO is still in place, Nvidia has technological advantages and a massive market-share lead that cannot be discounted. Given how expensive AMD stock is, I forecast that its stock will be flat over the next year and will still trade at around just under $600 per share at the end of 2027. Meanwhile, I wouldn't be surprised to see Nvidia's price-to-earnings ratio double to 20, which would also imply a stock price double that of today's level, about $330 per share.
